# Toast

A short message that confirms an action and goes away.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Brand expressive</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:brand-expressive;mode:light" title="Toast examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-toast--docs">Open Toast in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:brand-expressive;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Brand expressive:** Confirms a place on the waitlist.

- **Use it when:** Saved, sent, exported: something people should notice without stopping.
- **Not when:** A failure people must understand (alert or dialog), or a notice that stays (alert).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): Stays on the page.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): Needs an answer.

## Why it works this way

Toast looks the way it does because of 3 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Toast, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many tones does it use?</b><code>voice.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One per moment</div><p>Playful in headlines, plain in errors.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: A light note that something changed.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: Plain first, a light touch after: That didn't go through.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Badge: danger</code> <code>Alert: default</code> <code>Alert: destructive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Toast decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Headlines are short and bold. Three to six words.
- Verbs that move: Join, Try, Go.
- Playful in headlines, plain in errors.
- Use: Join, Drop, Go, Love. Avoid: Synergy, Leverage, Kindly.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Go
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Explore the drop

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is announced politely without taking focus, and stays long enough to read. undefined
- [ ] Nothing people must act on lives only in a toast. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toast
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
